1. How this register is to be used
This document serves two related purposes and the distinction between them governs what may be filed.

As a working register, it captures the full field of persons identified by the founding convenors as candidates for association with the Institute, whether as members of the profession, as honorary fellows, or as affiliates from adjacent disciplines. Candidates are drawn from the academic staff of the College of Art and Built Environment at KNUST, from the board, management and professional associates of Green Communities International, and from the academic and industry leaders who contributed to the International Conference on Environment, Social, Governance and Sustainable Development of Africa in 2024 and 2025.

As a statutory schedule, only a subset may be filed. The Registrar treats the list of members as a representation that the persons named are members at the date of application. A person who has not signed a membership application and accepted the code of conduct is not a member, and the disciplinary jurisdiction asserted in the constitution cannot attach to that person. Every entry therefore carries a consent status, and the schedule annexed to Form A is generated as the extract of consented entries on the cut off date.

The sequence is straightforward. Issue the invitation and application form. Record the signed acceptance. Change the consent status. Generate the filing extract. Nothing here should be filed ahead of that sequence.
2. Membership classes and the coverage calculation

Section 5(2) of NRCD 143 requires that the membership of a professional body represent at least seventy five per cent of all persons trained and qualified in the profession concerned. That is a ratio, and both terms of it move together. A qualified person who joins the Institute enters the numerator and the denominator; a qualified person who does not join enters the denominator alone. Enrolment is therefore never harmful. What is harmful is defining the profession so broadly that the denominator swells with practitioners the Institute has no claim to and no prospect of enrolling.
The constitution accordingly separates the classes of association into those that fall within the profession and those that do not. Only the professional grades enter the coverage calculation.

Two consequences follow, and both are deliberate. Architecture, planning and land economy colleagues are recorded as Affiliates rather than dropped, because their association carries real institutional value while their disciplines are occupied by the Ghana Institute of Architects, the Ghana Institute of Planners and the Ghana Institution of Surveyors, and the Registrar does not register more than one professional body per profession. The international academic leadership is recorded as Honorary Fellows constituting the International Advisory Council, which is a stronger relationship than ordinary membership and costs nothing on the ratio.
Classes shown are proposed rather than conferred. Admission rests with the Membership and Credentials Committee against the criteria in the constitution.
3. Coverage evidence: the postgraduate qualification pathway

The strength of this application rests on the Institute being able to show the Registrar an enumerable population rather than an estimate. The postgraduate programmes of the Department of Construction Technology and Management at KNUST provide exactly that, since they constitute the principal formal training pathway producing qualified persons in project assurance and forensics in Ghana.

The cumulative graduate roll of those programmes, certified by the Head of Department, is therefore proposed as the primary evidence of the denominator. An examining officer can verify a certified graduate roll. He cannot verify an assertion that there are approximately two hundred practitioners nationally, and an application founded on the second kind of statement invites a refusal, which is published and harder to unwind than a delay.

Three points on completing that table. Graduates count and current students do not, since a person in training is not yet trained and qualified within the meaning of section 5(2); current students should nonetheless be enrolled in the Graduate class as the pipeline of the Institute. The count must be established before the definition of the profession is finalised, because a profession comprising fewer than fifty qualified persons cannot be registered without presidential dispensation, and the workable range sits between roughly sixty and two hundred. And the survey of comparable programmes at other institutions should be done honestly and documented, since an incomplete denominator discovered later is more damaging than a larger one disclosed at the outset.

9. Search of the register of professional bodies

The register published by the ORC in August 2024 records eighty three registered professional bodies, of which forty were in good standing at 31 July 2024 and forty three were not, together with eleven newly registered bodies and four that requested removal on gaining chartered status by Act of Parliament. That register has been searched against the proposed definition of the profession.

No registered body claims project forensics or project assurance. The territory is open. Several entries nonetheless sit close enough to bear on the drafting, and one point about them should not be overlooked: a body that is not in good standing remains on the register and continues to occupy its profession. Non compliance does not free the field.
Project management is occupied and must not appear as the governing description of the profession
Occupied a second time; the Registrar evidently tolerates fine distinctions between related professions
Still occupies construction; the objects should not be framed around construction practice generally

A formal entity information search should nonetheless be lodged with the ORC on the specific name strings before filing, since the published list dates from July 2024 and eleven bodies were newly registered in that period alone.
The two bodies most often assumed to occupy expert determination in Ghana do not, and neither is a registered professional body.

The Chartered Institute of Arbitrators operates in Ghana through a Chapter formed in September 2022, administratively attached to the CIArb Nigeria Branch. It confers the grades of a United Kingdom charity and connects the dispute resolution community through events and training. It does not appear on the ORC register of professional bodies and asserts no jurisdiction over a Ghanaian profession. The Ghana Arbitration Centre is a private provider of arbitration services rather than a regulator, and likewise does not appear on the register.

The Alternative Dispute Resolution Act, 2010 (Act 798) provides for the settlement of disputes by arbitration, mediation and customary arbitration and establishes an ADR Centre. Expert determination is treated in practitioner commentary as one of the recognised ADR mechanisms, but the operative provisions of Act 798 do not regulate it as a distinct process, and no body holds a statutory monopoly over it.

The exposure that does exist is at registry level rather than statutory, and it comes from the Ghana National Association of ADR Practitioners, which is registered and in good standing. Dispute avoidance and expert determination have accordingly been removed from the definition of the profession on the face of this schedule. They are retained in the credential specification as competencies that Fellows may practise, which preserves the substance while removing the only credible ground of objection from an incumbent body.

One check remains and it is the one that governs everything else. Establish the cumulative graduate count across the MSc Project Forensics, MSc Value Management and MSc Project Cost Engineering and Management programmes. If the total qualified population falls below fifty, the application requires presidential dispensation under the fifty person proviso in NRCD 143, and the founding convenors should decide whether to seek it or to defer filing until a further cohort has graduated.
